lessons.title: Estimate the gradient of a curve
lessons.summary: Draw a tangent at a specified point, choose two points on that line and use the signed rise and run.
lessons.objective: Draw a tangent at a specified point, choose two points on that line and use the signed rise and run.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to find the gradient of a straight line from two points.
lessons.ideas:
The tangent is a straight line through the point that matches the local direction of the curve. Look just to the left and right of the point when lining up the ruler.

Use points on the line you drew. Pick easy-to-read points well apart, preferably at grid intersections. A shallow line might need quite a long run.

A line drawn by eye and coordinates read from a grid have limited precision. Your estimate should have the right sign and be supported by the line and the points you used.
lessons.method:
How do I place a ruler to draw the tangent?

Mark the point first. Follow the curve for a short distance near it and adjust the ruler until the line has the same direction there. Draw that line long enough to read two separated points.

Which two points should I use?

Find \(\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\). Keep the order of subtraction the same above and below the fraction bar. Count actual axis units rather than squares when the scales differ.

Why is my answer an estimate?

Draw the tangent with a ruler, give the two coordinates and show the gradient calculation. A falling tangent must give a negative gradient when read from left to right.
mistakes: Joining two distant points on the curve gives a secant and measures the change across an interval.
A point on the curve that is off the tangent cannot be used for this calculation.
Larger and smaller triangles drawn along the same tangent give the same gradient when you use the correct axis units and signs.

examples.title: Use two points on the same tangent
examples.question: Two measured points on a tangent at \(P\) are \(A(1,-4)\) and \(B(5,4)\). Calculate the gradient of the marked tangent.
examples.solution:
Go from A to B. The signed change in height is \(8\) and the change in x is \(4\).

Divide the change in height by the change in x. The gradient is \(2\).

examples.title: Measure a longer segment of a tangent
examples.question: For a drawn tangent at \(x=-2\), a point on the line is \((-4,2)\). Moving along the line to \(x=0\) gives a vertical change of \(-12\). What gradient does this estimate?
examples.solution:
The horizontal change is \(0-(-4)=4\).

Divide the signed vertical change \(-12\) by the horizontal change. This gives \(-3\).

examples.title: Read the signed rise and run
examples.question: A pupil moves 9 units right along a tangent. The line goes down 4 units. Find the gradient of the tangent exactly.
examples.solution:
The run is \(9\). The vertical change is \(-4\) because the line goes down.

Divide vertical change by horizontal change to get \(-\frac{4}{9}\).

lessons.title: Differentiate powers and sums
lessons.summary: Apply the power rule to polynomial terms with rational coefficients, then use the derivative to find a gradient.
lessons.objective: Apply the power rule to polynomial terms with rational coefficients, then use the derivative to find a gradient.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to find the gradient of a straight line from two points.
lessons.ideas:
For \(y=ax^n\) with positive whole-number exponent \(n\), use \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=anx^{n-1}\).

A term \(bx\) has constant gradient \(b\). A constant has zero gradient because its graph is horizontal.

The derivative is a rule for gradient. The original formula is a rule for height on the curve. Use the correct formula for the quantity you want.
lessons.method:
How do I differentiate one power of x?

Multiply the old coefficient by the old exponent. Then reduce the exponent by one. Fractions in the coefficient work in exactly the same way.

What happens to a term in x or a constant?

Differentiate each term separately, including its sign, and add the results. For example, \(y=2x^5-7x+3\) gives \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=10x^4-7\).

How do I get the gradient at a specific x?

Find \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\) first. Then substitute the x-coordinate. Use brackets around a negative value of x before squaring or cubing it.
mistakes: Keep the sign of the original coefficient. Reducing the exponent alone misses the factor from the old exponent.
The constant in the original formula does not stay in the derivative. A linear term becomes a constant.
Putting the x-value into the original expression gives y, not the gradient.

examples.title: Find the gradient function
examples.question: Given \(y=\frac{7}{2}x^5\), find \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\). Give the expression for the derivative.
examples.solution:
Multiply the coefficient of each power by its original exponent. Reduce the exponent by one. A term in x becomes its coefficient.

A constant contributes zero. Combine the remaining terms to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{35}{2}x^4\).

examples.title: Differentiate a constant
examples.question: Given \(y=54\), find \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\). Give the expression for the derivative.
examples.solution:
The graph is a horizontal line. Its y-value stays fixed as x changes.

Its gradient is always zero, so \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=0\).

examples.title: Find the exact gradient at a point
examples.question: The curve has equation \(y=3x^3-12x+9\). Find its gradient at \(x=5\).
examples.solution:
First differentiate to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=9x^2-12\).

Substitute \(x=5\) into this derivative. The gradient is \(213\).

lessons.title: Find stationary points
lessons.summary: Use a zero derivative to find stationary x-values and the original curve to find each matching y-coordinate.
lessons.objective: Use a zero derivative to find stationary x-values and the original curve to find each matching y-coordinate.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to find the gradient of a straight line from two points.
lessons.ideas:
A horizontal line has gradient zero. At a stationary point, \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=0\).

Use the derivative to find x. Use the curve equation to find y. These two substitutions have different purposes.

A cubic can yield a polynomial of degree two when differentiated. Its zero-gradient equation can have two different solutions.
lessons.method:
What does a horizontal tangent tell me?

Differentiate first and set the result equal to zero. Solve that equation for x. This gives where the tangent is horizontal.

How do I find both coordinates?

After finding a stationary x-value, put that x into the original equation and write the answer as an ordered pair.

What if the derivative has two zeros?

Solve the resulting equation. For instance, \(x^2=16\) gives both \(x=4\) and \(x=-4\). Find a separate y-value for each and keep the pairs matched.
mistakes: Setting y equal to zero finds where the graph meets the x-axis. The question about a horizontal tangent asks for a zero gradient.
The y-coordinate of a stationary point does not have to be zero.
A square root key gives the positive square root. Solving an equation with a squared x can also give a negative solution.

examples.title: Find every x-value where the tangent is horizontal
examples.question: At which values of \(x\) is the tangent to \(y=x^3-3x+2\) horizontal?
examples.solution:
Horizontal means \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=0\). Solve \(3x^2-3=0\).

Both \(-1\) and \(1\) satisfy that equation.

examples.title: Find both coordinates of a stationary point
examples.question: Find the coordinates of the stationary point on \(y=6x^2-24x+10\).
examples.solution:
Solve \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=12x-24=0\). It gives \(x=2\).

Substitute \(2\) into the original equation for y to find \(y=-14\).

The resulting coordinates are \((2,-14)\).

examples.title: Find the two stationary points of a cubic
examples.question: Find all stationary points of \(y=4x^3-192x-6\). Give both coordinate pairs.
examples.solution:
Set \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=12x^2-192\) to zero. The equation reduces to \(x^2=16\).

Both \(x=-4\) and \(x=4\) work. Substitute both into the equation for y separately.

The resulting coordinates are \((-4,506),\quad (4,-518)\).

lessons.title: Classify maxima and minima
lessons.summary: Use gradient signs or the second derivative to classify a stationary point as a local maximum or minimum.
lessons.objective: Use gradient signs or the second derivative to classify a stationary point as a local maximum or minimum.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to find the gradient of a straight line from two points.
lessons.ideas:
Read the curve from left to right. An increasing branch has positive gradient and a decreasing branch has negative gradient.

Choose a test x-value in the interval immediately on either side of the proposed stationary point. Avoid crossing a different stationary point.

Differentiate \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\) once more to get \(\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}\). Use this test only after you know the point is stationary.
lessons.method:
What does the graph do on either side?

Positive to negative gives a local maximum. Negative to positive gives a local minimum. The horizontal tangent at the point itself has gradient zero in both cases.

How do I use the first derivative to justify a turn?

Substitute each test value into \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\). Record the two signs and say whether the curve changes from rising to falling or falling to rising.

How can the second derivative distinguish the two?

At the stationary x-value, a positive \(\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}\) indicates a local minimum and a negative value indicates a local maximum. If it gives zero, check the first derivative on both sides or use a sketch.
mistakes: The sign of the y-coordinate tells you the height relative to the axis. It cannot tell you the nature of the stationary point.
Do not test only the stationary x-value. Its gradient is zero whether the point is a maximum or a minimum.
A positive second derivative at a stationary point means the slope is increasing through zero. That makes a minimum, even when the point is above the x-axis.

examples.title: Recognise a turn from gradient signs
examples.question:
The curve is smooth near \(x=8\). At this stationary point its tangent is horizontal. The gradient is \(-2\) just before it and \(5\) just after it. What is the nature of the point?

  1. Local minimum
  2. Local maximum
  3. The y-coordinate is zero.
  4. The gradient data cannot distinguish the two cases.
examples.solution:
The signed gradients go from negative to positive.

That means the curve turns at a local minimum.

examples.title: Test the gradient on both sides
examples.question:
The curve \(y=2x^3-24x+12\) has a stationary point at \(x=2\). Use the signs of the gradients just to either side. What is the nature of this stationary point?

  1. The information is insufficient to decide.
  2. Local minimum
  3. Local maximum
  4. The point is an x-intercept because its gradient is zero.
examples.solution:
Differentiate to find \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=6x^2-24\).

At \(\frac{3}{2}\) the gradient is \(-\frac{21}{2}\). At \(\frac{5}{2}\) it is \(\frac{27}{2}\).

The graph changes from decreasing to increasing. Therefore it is a local minimum.

examples.title: Use the second derivative at a stationary point
examples.question:
The curve \(y=-3x^3+81x+2\) has a stationary point at \(x=-3\). Use the second derivative. What is the nature of this stationary point?

  1. The point is an x-intercept because its gradient is zero.
  2. The information is insufficient to decide.
  3. Local minimum
  4. Local maximum
examples.solution:
The first derivative is \(-9x^2+81\). Differentiate it again to get \(\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}=-18x\).

At the stationary x-value this is \(54\). Its sign gives a local minimum.

lessons.title: Sketch curves using stationary points
lessons.summary: Combine the turning points, their types and the y-intercept into a sketch that shows the direction of each branch.
lessons.objective: Combine the turning points, their types and the y-intercept into a sketch that shows the direction of each branch.
lessons.before: For 0580 Extended. Recall how to find the gradient of a straight line from two points.
lessons.ideas:
Mark the axes, plot the stationary points and identify the y-intercept. Their relative positions make it easier to link the branches.

The derivative tells you where the graph rises or falls. Its sign in each interval fixes the direction of the branch there.

Read across the sketch in increasing x. Check that the curve has the calculated y-intercept and goes through each stationary point with the expected direction change.
lessons.method:
Which points should I put on the sketch first?

Find the stationary x-values from the derivative and their heights from the original formula. Use \(x=0\) in the original equation for the y-intercept.

Which way should the curve go between the turns?

An upward curve that turns down makes a local maximum. The next turn can reverse the direction again. Mark both types before joining the points with a smooth graph.

How can I check the completed sketch?

Label the stationary coordinates and name the types. A sketch does not require a table of many values, but it must show their relative positions and the local shape correctly.
mistakes: A stationary point is not automatically an intercept. Use all the information from your working.
Do not draw sharp corners at the stationary points. A differentiable graph has a horizontal tangent there.
Giving only the x-value of a maximum misses its height. Use the curve equation for the y-coordinate.

examples.title: Find the point where the sketch meets the y-axis
examples.question: For a sketch of \(y=-2x^3+24x-5\), find the y-intercept. Give its coordinates.
examples.solution:
On the y-axis, \(x=0\). Substitute into the original equation.

Every power of x vanishes. The constant gives \(y=-5\).

The resulting coordinates are \((0,-5)\).

examples.title: Choose an order for the turning points
examples.question:
The equation is \(y=x^3-3x+3\). The two turning points occur at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\) from left to right. Which order must the sketch show?

  1. The graph falls throughout.
  2. Maximum, then minimum
  3. Minimum, then maximum
  4. The graph rises throughout.
examples.solution:
The derivative has one sign between the two roots and the opposite sign outside. The graph goes up, then down, then up.

The turn order is maximum, then minimum.

examples.title: Find the height of the local maximum
examples.question: A sketch of \(y=2x^3-24x+6\) has turning points at \(x=\pm 2\). Find the y-value of the local maximum.
examples.solution:
The second derivative is \(12x\). It is negative at \(x=-2\), so this x gives the local maximum.

Substitute that x into the original equation to get \(y=38\).

questions.title: Draw and measure a tangent
questions.prompt_html:
1. The graph shows a curve and the point \(P(2,2)\). Use a ruler to draw a tangent to the curve at P and estimate its gradient. Show the coordinates used.

    [3]

  2. For a drawn tangent at \(x=-1\), a point on the line is \((-5,-11)\). Moving along the line to \(x=3\) gives a vertical change of \(12\). What gradient does this estimate?

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Draw a long straight line through P that follows the local direction of the curve. Read two clear points on that line.

For the illustrated tangent, the two points are \((0,-5)\) and \((4,9)\). Divide the signed rise by the run to get \(\frac{7}{2}\).

(b)

The horizontal change is \(3-(-5)=8\).

Divide the signed vertical change \(12\) by the horizontal change. This gives \(\frac{3}{2}\).
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Choose points well apart on your drawn tangent. Points on the curve are used only if they lie on the tangent as well.

(b)

The horizontal change uses both x-coordinates of the measurement.

marking_criteria.description_html: Draw a plausible tangent through P with a ruler.
Use two separated points on that line and calculate signed rise divided by run.
A defensible estimate within \(0.3\) of \(\frac{7}{2}\), supported by the tangent and working.
Subtract the two x-coordinates for the run and divide the stated rise by it.

1. Sketch \(y=-3x^3+81x+11\). Find and label both stationary points and their nature. Mark the y-intercept.

    [4]

  2. The curve \(y=-2x^3+24x-4\) has a stationary point at \(x=2\). Use the signs of the gradients just to either side. Determine its nature and show your working.

    [2]
questions.answer_html:
(a) Local minimum at \((-3,-151)\), local maximum at \((3,173)\), y-intercept \((0,11)\).

(b) Local maximum
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Differentiate and set the gradient equal to zero. This gives \(x^2=9\) and therefore \(x=\pm 3\).

Local minimum at \((-3,-151)\), local maximum at \((3,173)\), y-intercept \((0,11)\).

Draw the branches in the correct directions and use horizontal tangents at the two turns.

(b)

Differentiate to find \(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=-6x^2+24\).

At \(\frac{3}{2}\) the gradient is \(\frac{21}{2}\). At \(\frac{5}{2}\) it is \(-\frac{27}{2}\).

The graph changes from increasing to decreasing. Therefore it is a local maximum.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Calculate the two stationary points, then check the direction between the points and on either side.

(b)

Identify the requested method, and apply it at or around the stated stationary point as appropriate.

questions.title: Plot and justify the turns of a curve
questions.prompt_html:
1. The equation is \(y=2x^3-24x+6\). The two turning points occur at \(x=-2\) and \(x=2\) from left to right. State the order of maximum and minimum, with a reason.

    [2]

  2. Sketch \(y=2x^3-24x+11\). Find and label both stationary points and their nature. Mark the y-intercept.

    [4]
questions.answer_html:
(a) Maximum, then minimum

(b) Local maximum at \((-2,43)\), local minimum at \((2,-21)\), y-intercept \((0,11)\).
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The derivative has one sign between the two roots and the opposite sign outside. The graph goes up, then down, then up.

The turn order is maximum, then minimum.

(b)

Differentiate and set the gradient equal to zero. This gives \(x^2=4\) and therefore \(x=\pm 2\).

Local maximum at \((-2,43)\), local minimum at \((2,-21)\), y-intercept \((0,11)\).

Draw the branches in the correct directions and use horizontal tangents at the two turns.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Follow the curve from left to right through both stationary points.

(b)

Calculate the two stationary points, then check the direction between the points and on either side.
